title: What If the Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Hit Earth Today?

scenes.text: What if the dinosaur-killing asteroid hit Earth today? The first wave is the one that matters.
It was about 14 kilometers wide, and it hit at roughly 43,000 kilometers an hour.
Within three minutes, a wall of water about 4.5 kilometers tall rose around the crater.
Within 48 hours, waves hit most of Earth's coastlines, with up to 30,000 times the energy of the 2004 tsunami.
Then about 25 trillion tons of dust, ash and steam darkened the sky, causing a global winter.
Last time, about 75 percent of all species died out. The wave was just the beginning.

description:
What if the dinosaur-killing asteroid hit Earth today?
A 14 kilometer asteroid raised a wall of water about 4.5 kilometers tall within minutes, then dust darkened the sky.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which would scare you more, the wave or the dark years after? Drop your own what if.
